question.text:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by \[ A = \big\{ (x,y) \in\mathbb R^2 \,:\, -2 \leq x < 0, \, 0 < y \leq 1 \big\}. \]

The interior of $A$ is given by \[ \textrm{int}\,A = \big\{ (x,y) \in\mathbb R^2 \,:\, \bbox[5px, border: 1px solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}, \, 0 < y < 1 \, \big\}. \]

What is the missing expression?
question.explanation:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $\partial A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $\partial A$ are shown below.

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $ \textrm{int}\, A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: \[ \textrm{int}\,A = A - \partial A \]

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

So, in this case, the interior of $A$ is given by \[ \textrm{int}\,A = \big\{ (x,y) \in\mathbb R^2 \,:\, \bbox[5px, border: 1px solid black]{-2 < x < 0}, \, 0 < y < 1 \, \big\}. \]

example.title: Identifying the Interior of a Set

question.text: Consider the set $A$ shown above. The interior of $A$ is \[ \textrm{int}\,A = \big\{ (x,y)\in\mathbb R^2 \,:\, 0 \lt x \lt 1, \, \bbox[5px, border: 1px solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}} \big\}. \] What is the missing expression?
question.explanation:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $\partial A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $\partial A$ are shown below.

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $ \textrm{int}\, A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: \[ \textrm{int}\,A = A - \partial A \]

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

So, in this case, the interior of $A$ is given by

\[ \textrm{int}\,A = \big\{ (x,y)\in\mathbb R^2 \,:\, 0 \lt x \lt 1, \, \bbox[5px, border: 1px solid black]{-1 \lt y \lt 0} \big\}. \]

question.text: Consider the set $A,$ shown above. The boundary of $A$ is given by \[ \partial A = \big\{ (x,y) \in\mathbb R^2 \,:\, \bbox[5px, border: 1px solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}} \, \big\}. \] What is the missing expression?
question.explanation:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $\partial A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $\partial A$ are shown below.

From the diagram, the boundary points of $A$ lie on the parabola $2y = x^2.$

Therefore,

\[ \partial A = \big\{ (x,y) \in\mathbb R^2\,:\, \bbox[5px, border: 1px solid black]{2y = x^2} \, \big\}. \]

question.text:
Consider the set $A$ shown above. The interior of $A$ is

\[ \textrm{int}\,A = \big\{ (x,y) \in\mathbb R^2 \,:\, 4x^2+y^2 < 4, \, \bbox[5px, border: 1px solid black]{\phantom{AAAA}} \big\}. \]

What is the missing expression?
question.explanation:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $\partial A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $\partial A$ are shown below.

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $ \textrm{int}\, A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: \[ \textrm{int}\,A = A - \partial A \]

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

So, in this case, the interior of $A$ is given by

\[ \textrm{int}\,A = \big\{ (x,y) \in\mathbb R^2\,:\, 4x^2+y^2 < 4, \, \bbox[5px, border: 1px solid black]{0 < y < 2} \big\}. \]
